To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
10% to over one quarter of the US population may have inadequate nutrient intakes and that there are differences in nutrient intakes by race/ethnic group and by age.

10% to more than 25% of the population may habitually consume less than the RDA for some nutrients; Hispanics reported higher energy intake and a lower percentage energy from fat than other ethnic groups; and use of adjustment factors improved the accuracy of nutrient intake data from the questionnaire.
the 1987 NHIS food frequency questionnaire provides a valid estimate of the distribution (mean and variance) of nutrient intakes in the US adult population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a food frequency questionnaire for use in large-scale surveys.
the development of a short, self-administered food frequency questionnaire that provides estimates of nutrient intake that are comparable with those from more extensive dietary surveys.
the use of a food frequency questionnaire to estimate nutrient intake in a nationally representative population sample.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 1987 NHIS data on nutrient intake are useful for describing the distribution of nutrient intake among the general US population and for comparing nutrient intake in demographic subgroups.
the 1987 NHIS food frequency questionnaire provides reliable estimates of nutrient intake for a representative sample of adults 18 to years of age in the United States.

the food frequency questionnaire administered to a representative sample in the 1988 National Health Interview Survey is an acceptable instrument for assessing the distribution of nutrient intake in a national sample.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NHIS food frequency questionnaire provides a useful method for estimating the usual nutrient intake of US adults.
we were able to develop a shortened questionnaire that was able to provide estimates of usual nutrient intake in a national probability survey.

we have developed an approach for estimating nutrient intake distributions from a food frequency questionaire, and that this approach is useful for estimating nutrient intake in a national sample.
